title: Destructive Mothering: Son-Husbands and the Prevalence of Mommy Issues
author: Foster, Michael
summary: Michael Foster examines how certain patterns of mothering create men who are emotionally dependent on women, unable to exercise authority, and incapable of genuine leadership. When mothers fail to release their sons into manhood, treating them as eternal children or emotional support partners, they cripple the development of healthy masculinity. These 'mommy issues'—emotional enmeshment, maternal dominance, confusion about boundaries—produce men who cannot lead their own families or assume the responsibilities of adult manhood. Foster argues that mothers must understand that truly loving their sons means releasing them, setting firm boundaries, and respecting their developing independence and masculine identity.
points: Maternal emotional enmeshment prevents healthy masculine development in sons.
Sons who are treated as eternal children or emotional support partners cannot develop into effective leaders.
Mothers must understand that loving their sons includes releasing them into adulthood and independence.
The failure to properly separate from mothers produces men incapable of healthy adult relationships.
quotes: Son-husbands lack the capacity for genuine leadership because they never fully separated from maternal dominance.
A mother's task is not to keep her son dependent but to release him into manhood.
The mommy issues that plague modern men are the result of mothers who failed to set proper boundaries.” Archived from We Made People Substack on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
